title: Trace a progressive rollout and rollback
description: Switch release stages to see which path serves customers, where evidence is collected, and how a breached gate returns traffic to the stable version. Select any component for its responsibility.

nodes.label: Customer cohort
nodes.detail: A named cohort keeps the canary measurable. It may be a region, tenant group, internal users, or a random but logged percentage of eligible traffic.

nodes.label: Edge router
nodes.detail: Applies the rollout policy and records which version served the request. It must support freezing or reversing traffic without deploying another binary.

nodes.label: Stable version
nodes.detail: Serves the established path and supplies the comparison baseline for errors, latency, saturation, and customer outcomes.

nodes.label: Canary version
nodes.detail: Receives only the permitted cohort. Its code and data behavior must remain compatible with the stable version while both are live.

nodes.label: Release gate
nodes.detail: Evaluates a fixed observation window against a stable baseline and explicit thresholds. It is an evidence source, not an automated excuse to ignore a customer regression.

nodes.label: Rollback control
nodes.detail: Freezes promotion and updates routing or the emergency flag. It protects new requests first; reconciliation handles any state that the failed version already changed.

scenarios.label: Shadow comparison
scenarios.summary: Customers receive the stable response while eligible requests are mirrored to the candidate outside the response path. Candidate output can be compared without broad user exposure.
scenarios.result: Shadowing exposes production input diversity, but it does not prove the customer experience. Isolate writes and downstream effects before mirroring a request.

scenarios.label: 1% healthy canary
scenarios.summary: A small logged cohort receives the candidate while the remaining customers stay on the stable version. The release gate compares both groups over the observation window.
scenarios.result: Promote only if technical guardrails and the named customer outcome stay within threshold. A green aggregate dashboard can still hide a harmful cohort.

scenarios.label: 10% guardrail breach
scenarios.summary: At a larger canary stage, candidate errors and checkout failures exceed the allowed difference from stable. The gate emits a breach instead of permitting the next traffic increase.
scenarios.result: Do not continue collecting evidence on more customers. Freeze the rollout and execute the route-back while request, version, and cohort evidence is still available.

scenarios.label: Rollback complete
scenarios.summary: The rollback control has removed the candidate from new customer traffic. The stable version serves the cohort while the incident owner investigates and assesses any writes made before the route-back.
scenarios.result: Customer exposure stops at the router. The remaining work is diagnosis, data reconciliation, and a forward-compatible fix; do not redeploy the same change only because traffic is stable again.
